elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 as redlined still provides that the Agreement "shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date" — there is no mutual-written-agreement default, and the automatic-renewal conditions are not all satisfied (opt-out is 60 days, not ≤30, and there is no vendor reminder), so this gateway element fails.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: "automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date" — each renewal term is 12 months; no multi-year rollover.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Redline sets the Company's window at "60 days written notice to HDI" — double the 30-day preferred ceiling. To reach preferred the operative text must read "thirty (30) days" for the Company's non-renewal/termination notice.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears anywhere in Section 4.1 as rendered; the margin comment acknowledges the reminder is absent ("preferred is 30 days plus an HDI reminder 60 days before renewal"). A promise in the comment is not operative language — an express sentence such as "HDI shall notify the Company in writing at least sixty (60) days prior to each renewal date" is required.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the only pricing term, Section 3.1, fixes consideration at "thirty percent (30%) of the Net Sales in excess of Eleven Thousand Dollars ($11,000) per calendar month," and Section 4.1 contains no uplift, re-pricing, or list-price mechanic on renewal, so no increase is permitted that would need capping.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Redlined Section 4.1: "unless terminated by the Company upon 60 days written notice to HDI" — the Company (Customer) stops the automatic renewal on 60 days, exactly at the fallback ceiling (down from the original mutual "ninety (90) days"). Deterministic check confirms value=60.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: renewal is at the same fixed revenue-share fee (Section 3.1, 30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month) with no renewal uplift language, so there is no increase to cap.

reasons: Fallback is complete: the single edit moves the Customer's non-renewal window from 90 to 60 days, and the price-cap element is satisfied by inapplicability because Section 3.1 fixes the fee (30% of Net Sales over $11,000/month) with no renewal uplift mechanic. The finding is correctly scored a deviation against the original 90-day window and correctly targets the fallback.

Preferred remains out of reach for three named gaps, each of which would need operative text, not comment text: (1) the Company's opt-out is 60 days rather than "thirty (30) days"; (2) there is no HDI obligation to notify the Company at least sixty (60) days before each renewal date; (3) with those conditions unmet, the mutual-written-agreement default is not displaced. These are gaps short of preferred wording, not independent deviations, so noting them in the rationale (as the drafter did) is the right treatment.

Minimality holds: only the notice phrase in the second sentence of Section 4.1 changed. The 12-month renewal term, the Effective Date trigger, the "Such notice shall specify the date..." sentence and the "Termination Date" definition, Section 3.1 pricing, and the Section 4.2 Termination Payment are all untouched, and HDI's 90-day exit notice is deliberately retained as favourable existing language (transition runway for us). No requirement outside the fallback checklist was added.

Intent preserved: the clause still operates as a combined term/automatic-renewal/notice provision with reciprocal (now asymmetric, in our favour) exit notice; nothing contradicts the Section 4.2 termination-payment mechanic or the revenue-share economics. Because the same sentence carries both the non-renewal and the termination-notice function, shortening the Company's side is the only way to reach the fallback and its incidental effect on our own exit notice benefits us and should not be flagged.

Drafting nits to clean up (non-blocking, do not affect level completeness): render the new figure as "sixty (60) days" to match the numeral-plus-words convention used for "ninety (90) days" in the same sentence, and restore the addressee on HDI's leg ("by HDI upon ninety (90) days written notice to the Company") since the redline dropped the original "to the other."
